query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a ductile phase, such as a metallic glass, into the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy can enhance its load-bearing integrity without compromising its caloric performance.
generation.intervention: Incorporation of a ductile metallic glass phase
generation.mechanism: Enhanced toughness and resistance to cracking due to the ductile phase
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved load-bearing integrity and preserved caloric performance
generation.boundary: Operating temperatures between 250 K and 350 K, magnetic fields up to 5 Tesla, and pressures up to 100 MPa
generation.uncertainty: The optimal composition and distribution of the ductile phase are unknown

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of the caloric response and mechanical properties of the modified alloy with the as-cast alloy under identical operating conditions
measurements: Magnetization, entropy change, and mechanical stress-strain curves
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the modified alloy exhibits a significant decrease in caloric performance or no improvement in load-bearing integrity compared to the as-cast alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
